title: Kenyan Beef Stir Fry
community: Popular across Kenya — especially in urban households
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Beef Stir Fry — thin strips of tender beef quickly fried at high heat with onions, garlic, ginger, tomatoes, and colourful bell peppers in a fragrant Kenyan spice blend. Fast, bold, and satisfying.
longDesc: Kenyan beef stir fry is not the same as Chinese stir fry — it uses Kenyan spices and a tomato base rather than soy sauce, giving it a distinctly East African character. Quick to make and deeply satisfying, it has become a popular weeknight dish in urban Kenyan households.
ingredients: 500g beef sirloin — cut into thin strips against the grain
steps: Slice beef thinly against the grain. Season with salt, pepper, and paprika.
Heat oil in a wok or large pan over very high heat until smoking.
Add beef strips in a single layer. Sear for 1—2 minutes without stirring. Toss and cook another 1 minute. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, add onions and peppers. Stir-fry for 3—4 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger. Cook 30 seconds.
Add tomatoes, cumin, and chilli flakes. Cook for 3—4 minutes.
Return the beef. Add soy sauce if using. Toss everything together and cook for 2 more minutes.
Squeeze over lemon juice, scatter with coriander, and serve immediately.
chefTips: Slice beef against the grain — this shortens the muscle fibres and ensures tenderness.
The pan must be very hot before the beef goes in — this is what gives stir fry its character.
Cook the beef first and remove it — returning at the end prevents overcooking.
commonMistakes: Cold pan — produces grey, steamed beef rather than caramelised strips.
Crowding the pan — lowers temperature and causes steaming.
Cutting with the grain — makes the beef chewy.

faqs.a: Courgette, broccoli, mushrooms, snap peas, and carrots all work well. Add harder vegetables first and softer ones towards the end.

cookingScience: Cutting against the grain reduces muscle fibre length in each bite, making the beef tender even when cooked quickly. High-heat stir-frying achieves the Maillard reaction rapidly, creating caramelised flavour in seconds.
sustainabilityTips: Stir fry is ideal for using up vegetables before they spoil.
storage: Best eaten immediately. Refrigerate for up to 2 days.
reheating: Reheat quickly in a hot pan.
healthBenefits: Bell peppers provide high amounts of vitamin C.
Quick cooking preserves more nutrients than long simmering.
culturalNote: Beef stir fry has become increasingly popular in urban Kenyan households as a quick, flavourful weeknight meal that uses minimal time and ingredients.
regionalVariations: Asian-Kenyan fusion — with soy and oyster sauce.
Stir fry with ugali — a modern Kenyan comfort pairing.
